As the summer unfolds, Sarah must navigate complex relationships, heal old wounds, and decide if she can find forgiveness and a new beginning in the place she once called home.

title: Peek-a-Boo! (Babyfaces)
author: Roberta Grobel Intrater
motif: Peek-a-boo, Faces, Emotions
tags: Babies, Toddlers, Interaction, Learning
blurb: Peek-a-Boo! (Babyfaces) by Roberta Grobel Intrater is a delightful board book designed for the youngest readers. Through simple, engaging photographs of diverse babies, the book invites little ones to participate in the classic game of peek-a-boo. Each page reveals a new baby's face, often with a playful expression, encouraging interaction and recognition. The sturdy pages are perfect for tiny hands, making it an ideal first book for babies and toddlers. It's a wonderful tool for parents and caregivers to share moments of joy, connection, and early learning, fostering language development and emotional understanding through familiar faces and playful discovery.

title: The BFG: A Set of Plays
author: Roald Dahl/David Wood
themes: Friendship, Courage, Good vs. Evil, Imagination
motif: Giants, Dreams, Whistleblowing, Orphanhood
tags: Roald Dahl, BFG, Stage Play, Children's Story
blurb: This collection presents 'The BFG: A Set of Plays,' adapted by David Wood from Roald Dahl's beloved novel. It brings to life the enchanting story of Sophie, a young orphan who befriends the Big Friendly Giant. Together, they embark on a thrilling adventure to save England from the cannibalistic giants. The plays capture the magic, humor, and heartwarming themes of friendship and bravery that have made Dahl's work a timeless classic for young audiences. Perfect for stage productions, this adaptation retains the whimsical charm and imaginative spirit of the original story, offering a delightful theatrical experience.

title: Science Notebooks: Writing about Inquiry
author: Lori Fulton/Brian Campbell/Linda Gregg
themes: Inquiry-Based Learning, Scientific Literacy, Student Voice, Teacher Professional Development
motif: Observation, Documentation, Reflection, Communication
category: Curriculum Development, Teaching Strategies, Classroom Practice
tags: Science Notebooks, Inquiry, Writing in Science, Elementary Education
blurb: This book offers a comprehensive guide to implementing and utilizing science notebooks as a powerful tool for fostering inquiry-based learning in elementary classrooms. Authors Lori Fulton, Brian Campbell, and Linda Gregg provide practical strategies and research-based insights for teachers to effectively integrate writing into science instruction. The book emphasizes how science notebooks can serve as a space for students to document observations, record data, formulate questions, and reflect on their scientific thinking. It highlights the importance of student voice and the role of notebooks in developing scientific literacy and a deeper understanding of scientific concepts.  The resource is designed to support teachers in creating a dynamic and engaging science learning environment.

title: Interviews with John Kenneth Galbraith (Conversations with Public Intellectuals)
author: John Kenneth Galbraith/James Ronald Stanfield/J. Ron Stanfield/Jacqueline Bloom Stanfield
themes: Economic Theory, Political Commentary, Social Critique, Intellectual History
motif: Power Structures, Inequality, Consumerism, Public Policy
tags: Economics, Politics, Society, Galbraith
blurb: This collection of interviews offers a profound glimpse into the mind of John Kenneth Galbraith, one of the most influential economists and public intellectuals of the 20th century. Through conversations with James Ronald Stanfield and Jacqueline Bloom Stanfield, Galbraith elaborates on his seminal ideas concerning economic power, the influence of advertising, the nature of inequality, and the role of government. The book delves into his critiques of conventional economic wisdom and his insights into the social and political forces shaping modern capitalism. It serves as an accessible yet rigorous exploration of his enduring legacy and his continued relevance to understanding contemporary economic and social issues.

title: The Economics of Innocent Fraud: Truth for Our Time
author: John Kenneth Galbraith
themes: Deception, Power Structures, Social Inequality, Economic Systems
motif: Illusion, Manipulation, Conventional Wisdom, Social Norms
tags: Capitalism, Corporate Power, Public Perception, Economic Theory
blurb: John Kenneth Galbraith's 'The Economics of Innocent Fraud' dissects the pervasive, often unconscious, deceptions that underpin modern economic and social systems. He argues that 'innocent fraud' – the polite fictions and accepted untruths that allow powerful interests to maintain their position – is not malicious but a necessary lubricant for the smooth functioning of society. Galbraith examines how these illusions, from the concept of the 'sovereign consumer' to the justifications for extreme wealth, are perpetuated and accepted. The book is a critical examination of how conventional wisdom and self-interest conspire to obscure reality, leading to a society that often operates on a foundation of accepted falsehoods. It's a call to recognize and challenge these ingrained deceptions for a more truthful understanding of our economic world.

title: Robin Williams Web Design Workshop
author: Robin P. Williams/John Tollett/Dave Rohr
themes: Web Design, User Interface, User Experience
motif: Practical Application, Skill Development, Creative Process
tags: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Web Development
blurb: This workshop-style book by Robin P. Williams, John Tollett, and Dave Rohr offers a hands-on approach to learning web design. It guides readers through the fundamental principles and practical techniques required to build effective and engaging websites. Covering essential technologies like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the book emphasizes a user-centered design philosophy, focusing on creating intuitive interfaces and positive user experiences. Through exercises and real-world examples, aspiring web designers can develop the skills needed to translate creative ideas into functional and visually appealing online presences. It's an ideal resource for beginners and those looking to solidify their understanding of modern web development practices.

title: The Non-Designer's Web Book
author: Robin P. Williams/John Tollett
motif: Clarity, Consistency, Visual Hierarchy, Readability
tags: Web Design, Graphic Design, User Interface, User Experience
blurb: The Non-Designer's Web Book is a foundational guide for anyone looking to create effective and visually appealing websites without a formal design background. Authors Robin P. Williams and John Tollett break down complex design principles into easily digestible concepts, focusing on core elements like contrast, repetition, alignment, and proximity. The book emphasizes creating user-friendly and accessible web experiences, guiding readers through practical advice on layout, typography, color, and imagery. It empowers individuals to make informed design decisions, transforming cluttered or unprofessional websites into clear, engaging, and professional online presences. This accessible resource is ideal for small business owners, bloggers, and anyone seeking to improve their web design skills.

title: Hard Drive: Bill Gates and the Making of the Microsoft Empire
author: James Wallace/Jim  Erickson
motif: Disruption, Ambition, Control, Legacy
category: Business History, Technological Advancement, Corporate Biography, Personal Development
tags: Microsoft, Bill Gates, Software Industry, Personal Computing
blurb: This book chronicles the meteoric rise of Bill Gates and Microsoft, detailing their early days, strategic decisions, and relentless pursuit of dominance in the personal computer software market. It explores the intense competition, the innovative spirit, and the sometimes ruthless tactics that propelled Microsoft to become a global technology empire.  'Hard Drive' offers an in-depth look at the personalities, the challenges, and the pivotal moments that shaped the digital landscape we know today, with a particular focus on the visionary and often controversial figure of Bill Gates.

title: Bill Gates: Computer Legend (Famous Lives)
author: Sara Barton-Wood
motif: American Dream, Visionary Leadership, Business Acumen
tags: Computers, Software, Microsoft, Bill Gates
blurb: This biography explores the life and achievements of Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft. It details his early fascination with computers, the founding of Microsoft, and its rise to become a dominant force in the software industry. The book highlights Gates's business strategies, his impact on personal computing, and his later transition into philanthropy through the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Aimed at young readers, it offers an accessible look at a pivotal figure in modern technological history and his enduring legacy.

title: Chicken Trek
author: Stephen Manes
motif: Journey, Overcoming Obstacles, Animal Communication
tags: Chickens, Farm Animals, Road Trip, Escape
blurb: In Stephen Manes' 'Chicken Trek,' a group of determined chickens embarks on an extraordinary journey to escape their farm and find a better life. Led by the brave and resourceful Henrietta, these feathered friends face a world far larger and more dangerous than they ever imagined. From the familiar confines of the coop to the unpredictable wilds, they must rely on their wits, their courage, and their unwavering bond to overcome predators, navigate unfamiliar landscapes, and outsmart those who would keep them captive. This heartwarming adventure celebrates the power of friendship and the indomitable spirit of even the smallest creatures in their quest for freedom and a place to call home.

title: Make Four Million Dollars by Next Thursday!
author: Stephen Manes/George Ulrich
motif: Get-Rich-Quick Schemes, Financial Advice, Business Strategy
tags: Business, Finance, Entrepreneurship, Humor
blurb: This satirical guide, 'Make Four Million Dollars by Next Thursday!', by Stephen Manes and George Ulrich, hilariously dissects the often-absurd world of get-rich-quick schemes and aggressive business advice. Through a fictional narrative, it exposes the unrealistic promises and questionable strategies peddled in the pursuit of rapid wealth. The book serves as a cautionary tale, humorously highlighting the importance of realistic financial planning, sound business principles, and a healthy dose of skepticism when faced with seemingly effortless paths to riches. It's a witty commentary on entrepreneurial ambition and the allure of overnight success.

title: Slim Down Camp
author: Stephen Manes
themes: Body Image, Self-Esteem, Friendship, Family Dynamics
motif: Transformation, Acceptance, Overcoming Challenges, Social Pressure
category: Coming-of-Age, Social Issues, Health and Wellness
tags: Weight Loss, Teen Issues, Summer Camp, Personal Growth
blurb: Twelve-year-old Kevin is sent to 'Slim Down Camp' by his parents, who are concerned about his weight. Initially resistant and embarrassed, Kevin finds himself navigating the challenges of a strict diet, intense physical activity, and the social dynamics of a camp filled with other kids struggling with similar issues. As he forms unexpected friendships and confronts his own insecurities, Kevin begins to question the true meaning of health and self-acceptance, realizing that the camp's focus might be on more than just shedding pounds. 'Slim Down Camp' explores the pressures of body image and the journey towards finding confidence and belonging.

title: The Boy Who Turned Into a TV Set
author: Stephen Manes/Michael  Bass
motif: Transformation, Media Consumption, Escapism
tags: Humor, Satire, Coming-of-Age, Social Commentary
blurb: In Stephen Manes and Michael Bass's quirky novel, 'The Boy Who Turned Into a TV Set,' young Kevin discovers a bizarre and unsettling transformation: he's slowly turning into a television set. As his body morphs into a cathode ray tube and his thoughts become filled with static and programming, Kevin must grapple with his changing identity and the overwhelming influence of media. This humorous yet thought-provoking story explores themes of escapism, the impact of television on childhood, and the struggle to maintain one's individuality in a world saturated with entertainment. Kevin's surreal journey is a commentary on how technology can both connect and isolate us, forcing him and his family to confront what it truly means to be human.

title: Masters of Enterprise: Giants of American Business from John Jacob Astor and J.P. Morgan to Bill Gates and Oprah Winfrey
author: H.W. Brands
motif: American Dream, Industrial Revolution, Technological Advancement, Media Influence
category: Business Leaders, Historical Figures, Economic History
tags: American Business, Titans of Industry, Economic Power, Entrepreneurial Spirit
blurb: H.W. Brands' 'Masters of Enterprise' chronicles the lives and impact of America's most influential business leaders, from the early pioneers like John Jacob Astor and J.P. Morgan to modern titans like Bill Gates and Oprah Winfrey. The book explores the driving forces behind their success, their innovative strategies, and their profound influence on the American economy and society. It delves into the evolution of American capitalism, highlighting the entrepreneurial spirit, the pursuit of the American Dream, and the enduring legacies of these giants who shaped industries and redefined the landscape of business.

title: The Devil in the Junior League
author: Linda Francis Lee
themes: Social Climbing, Deception, Redemption, Class Differences
motif: Appearances vs. Reality, Secrets, Second Chances, Southern Society
tags: Humor, Relationships, Family, Small Town
blurb: In the seemingly idyllic world of the Junior League, where appearances are everything, a woman with a hidden past tries to reinvent herself. As she navigates the intricate social landscape, she finds herself entangled in secrets, lies, and unexpected romance.  'The Devil in the Junior League' explores the lengths people will go to for acceptance and the possibility of finding love and forgiveness, even when their true selves are at stake. It's a witty and heartwarming tale of second chances set against the backdrop of Southern charm and societal expectations.

title: Prom Anonymous
author: Blake Nelson
motif: Anonymity, Digital Communication, Social Media, Belonging
tags: Teenage Angst, Social Networks, Peer Pressure, Self-Discovery
blurb: In Blake Nelson's 'Prom Anonymous,' a group of high school students navigates the treacherous landscape of adolescence and social hierarchy.  When a mysterious online platform allows them to anonymously express their true feelings and desires, the lines between reality and digital persona blur.  As secrets are revealed and reputations are made and broken, the characters grapple with the consequences of their online actions and the struggle to find genuine connection in a world obsessed with appearances.  The novel explores themes of identity, conformity, and the isolating nature of modern technology, all set against the backdrop of the quintessential high school experience.

title: The New Rules of High School
author: Blake Nelson
motif: Cliques, Popularity, Social Pressure, Authenticity
category: Teen Fiction, Social Commentary, School Life
tags: High School, Social Dynamics, Teen Angst, Peer Pressure
blurb: Blake Nelson's 'The New Rules of High School' plunges into the brutal social landscape of American high school, dissecting the unspoken codes and hierarchies that govern teenage life. The novel follows a protagonist navigating the treacherous waters of popularity, conformity, and the desperate search for belonging. It's a raw and unflinching look at the pressures to fit in, the consequences of rebellion, and the often-painful process of discovering one's true self amidst the relentless judgment of peers. Nelson captures the anxieties and aspirations of adolescence with stark realism, offering a compelling, albeit bleak, portrait of the high school experience.

title: They Came from Below
author: Blake Nelson
motif: The Unknown, Transformation, Loss of Control, Environmental Threat
tags: Monsters, Conspiracy, Psychological Horror, Environmental Horror
blurb: In Blake Nelson's 'They Came from Below,' a remote, isolated community is plunged into terror when strange, subterranean creatures begin to emerge. As the inhabitants grapple with the horrifying reality of an unknown threat, paranoia and suspicion spread faster than the encroaching darkness. The novel masterfully blends elements of body horror and psychological suspense, exploring themes of isolation, the breakdown of trust, and the primal instinct for survival. As the line between human and monstrous blurs, the characters must confront not only the external horror but also the darkness within themselves as they fight to escape the encroaching doom from below.

title: User
author: Blake Nelson
motif: Technology, Conformity, Superficiality, Rebellion
tags: Teenage Angst, Internet Culture, Social Critique, Existentialism
blurb: Blake Nelson's 'User' plunges into the disaffected world of a suburban teenager navigating the nascent landscape of the internet and its impact on identity. As the protagonist grapples with alienation and the pressure to conform, he finds solace and a sense of self in the burgeoning online communities. The novel satirizes consumer culture and the superficiality of modern life, exploring how technology can both connect and isolate individuals. 'User' is a poignant and often darkly humorous examination of adolescence in an increasingly digitized world, questioning what it means to be real when so much of life is lived online.

title: Exile
author: Blake Nelson/Francine Kass
themes: Identity, Belonging, Social Alienation, Family Dynamics
motif: Music, Rebellion, Escape, Isolation
tags: Teenage Angst, Music Scene, Parental Conflict, Social Outcasts
blurb: In Blake Nelson's 'Exile,' a disillusioned teenager navigates the complexities of suburban life, finding solace and a sense of identity within the underground music scene. The novel delves into themes of social alienation, the struggle for belonging, and the often-strained relationships between parents and their children. As the protagonist grapples with his own sense of self, he finds a temporary refuge in the raw energy of punk rock and the camaraderie of fellow outsiders. 'Exile' is a poignant exploration of teenage rebellion, the search for meaning, and the enduring power of music to connect those who feel adrift in a world that doesn't quite understand them.

title: Girl (Girl  #1)
author: Blake Nelson
motif: Conformity vs. Individuality, Teenage Angst, Societal Expectations
tags: Teenage Life, High School, Social Commentary, Self-Discovery
blurb: Blake Nelson's 'Girl' plunges into the turbulent world of a teenage girl navigating the complexities of adolescence in suburban America. The novel explores the intense pressures of fitting in, the burgeoning awareness of sexuality, and the often-confusing journey of self-discovery. Through the eyes of its unnamed protagonist, the book captures the raw emotions, anxieties, and desires of youth as they grapple with societal expectations and the search for their own identity. It's a stark and honest portrayal of the challenges faced by young people on the cusp of adulthood.

title: My Side of the Mountain (Mountain  #1)
author: Jean Craighead George
motif: Wilderness, Solitude, Animal Companionship, Ingenuity
tags: Survival Skills, Nature Study, Family, Personal Growth
blurb: Sam Gribley, a young boy yearning for independence, escapes his crowded New York City apartment to live in the wilderness of the Catskill Mountains. Armed with his grandfather's penknife and a few basic supplies, Sam learns to survive by foraging, hunting, and building his own shelter. He befriends a falcon named Frightful and navigates the challenges of solitude and self-sufficiency. 'My Side of the Mountain' is a classic tale of a boy's quest for freedom and his deep connection with the natural world, showcasing his resourcefulness and resilience as he carves out his own life in the wild.

title: The Theban Plays: Oedipus Rex  Oedipus at Colonus & Antigone
author: Sophocles/George      Young
themes: Fate vs. Free Will, Justice and Law, Family and Duty, Divine Will
motif: Prophecy, Blindness, Guilt and Punishment, Suffering
category: Mythology, Ancient Greek Literature, Philosophical Fiction
tags: Greek Mythology, Sophocles, Oedipus, Antigone, Classical Tragedy
blurb: Sophocles' Theban Plays, comprising 'Oedipus Rex,' 'Oedipus at Colonus,' and 'Antigone,' offer a profound exploration of fate, free will, and the devastating consequences of human actions. These timeless tragedies follow the cursed lineage of Oedipus, from his unwitting parricide and incest to his exile and the subsequent defiance of his daughter, Antigone, against tyrannical law. The plays delve into themes of divine prophecy, the nature of justice, the burden of guilt, and the enduring power of familial bonds, all set against the backdrop of ancient Greek myth and societal structures. They remain a cornerstone of Western literature, prompting contemplation on the human condition and the inescapable forces that shape our lives.

title: The Jungle
author: Upton Sinclair/Earl Lee/Kathleen DeGrave
genres: Social Realism, Historical Fiction, Political Fiction
motif: The American Dream, Industrialization, Animalism, The Meat Industry
category: Social Commentary, Historical Novel, Investigative Journalism
tags: Labor Rights, Food Safety, Capitalism, Immigrant Experience
blurb: Upton Sinclair's 'The Jungle' is a searing indictment of the American meatpacking industry and the brutal realities faced by immigrant workers in early 20th-century Chicago. The novel follows the arduous journey of Jurgis Rudkus and his family as they arrive in America seeking opportunity, only to be ensnared in a cycle of exploitation, poverty, and unsanitary working conditions. Sinclair meticulously details the horrific practices within the slaughterhouses, exposing the corruption and greed that prioritized profit over human health and dignity. The book's graphic descriptions of spoiled meat and unsanitary processing shocked the public and spurred significant reforms in food safety legislation.

title: The Jungle Books
author: Rudyard Kipling/Alev Lytle Croutier
themes: Nature vs. Civilization, Law and Order, Belonging, Identity
motif: The Law of the Jungle, Animal Societies, Coming-of-Age, Survival
tags: Wildlife, Morality, Social Structures, Human-Animal Relations
blurb: Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Books' are a collection of enchanting tales set in the Indian jungle. The most famous stories follow Mowgli, a human boy raised by wolves, who navigates the complex laws and social structures of the animal kingdom. Through Mowgli's adventures, Kipling explores themes of nature versus civilization, the importance of belonging, and the struggle for identity. The books also feature standalone stories about other animals, offering moral lessons and insights into the wild. These timeless fables continue to captivate readers with their vivid imagery and profound observations on life.

title: Human Croquet
author: Kate Atkinson
genres: Magical Realism, Literary Fiction, Family Saga
themes: Memory, Identity, Family Secrets, The Unreliable Narrator
motif: Mirrors, Ghosts, Childhood Trauma, The Passage of Time
tags: Nostalgia, Surrealism, Intergenerational Trauma, Character Study
blurb: In Kate Atkinson's 'Human Croquet,' Isobel Fairfax navigates a childhood steeped in mystery and the uncanny. As she grows, the boundaries between reality and imagination blur, revealing a tapestry of family secrets, fragmented memories, and the lingering presence of the past. Isobel's journey is a poignant exploration of identity, the unreliability of perception, and the enduring impact of unspoken truths. The novel weaves a spellbinding narrative, where the ordinary is infused with the extraordinary, and the echoes of history shape the present.

title: The Key to Rebecca
author: Ken Follett/Arto Häilä
motif: Deception, Sacrifice, Duty, Survival
tags: World War II, Spies, North Africa, Espionage
blurb: In the heart of World War II, a brilliant German spy, codenamed 'Rebecca,' infiltrates Cairo with a mission to uncover vital Allied secrets. Her success could tip the scales of the war. Standing in her way is Major Alex Randall, a determined British intelligence officer tasked with finding and stopping her. As their paths converge, a dangerous game of cat and mouse unfolds, fraught with deception, betrayal, and unexpected romance. Randall must race against time to expose Rebecca before her intelligence reaches the Nazi high command, potentially altering the course of history.

title: Paper Money
author: Ken Follett
motif: Deception, Conspiracy, High Stakes, Justice
tags: Banking, Espionage, Organized Crime, International Finance
blurb: In Ken Follett's 'Paper Money,' a brilliant but ruthless financier orchestrates a complex scheme to manipulate the global stock market, aiming to bankrupt a powerful conglomerate and seize control. As his intricate plan unfolds, it draws in a diverse cast of characters, from ambitious bankers and desperate investors to determined law enforcement agents and shadowy figures from the criminal underworld. The novel plunges into the cutthroat world of high finance, where fortunes are made and lost in an instant, and where the pursuit of wealth often leads to dangerous alliances and deadly consequences. Follett masterfully weaves a tale of suspense, intrigue, and betrayal, exploring the corrupting influence of money and the lengths to which people will go to achieve ultimate power.

As they race against time and a formidable enemy, Cabrillo and his crew must navigate treacherous waters, decipher ancient clues, and confront their own pasts to prevent a global catastrophe. The Skeleton Coast of Oregon becomes a battleground for a secret that could rewrite history.

Cabrillo and his crew must race against time, navigating treacherous waters and uncovering a centuries-old conspiracy.  Their mission takes them from the rugged coast of Oregon to the icy expanses of the Arctic, facing deadly adversaries and the ghosts of the past.  The fate of the world hinges on their ability to decipher ancient clues and prevent the artifact from falling into the wrong hands.

Facing treacherous seas, Soviet agents, and the ghosts of the past, Pitt must overcome immense technical challenges and deadly adversaries to secure the future of the free world. This thrilling adventure combines historical intrigue with cutting-edge technology and high-octane action.
